summary: Adding provider "kimi" touches two orthogonal planes. Plane A is the deterministic router (agent_router.py + farm_state.sqlite agent_registry/agent_tasks), which decides which lane CLAIMS a ticket by a capability-subset filter then cost_rank ordering. Plane B is execution: run_agent_orchestration_task.py (the scheduled orchestration lane, per-agent hardcoded branches) and agent_chain.py (creator/critic/formatter chain, vendor switch in run_seat). A kimi lane declaring ONLY the 8 requested capabilities is UNROUTABLE: none appear in TASK_TYPE_CAPABILITIES, so no task ever requires them; a capability becomes routable only via a task_type, a payload required_capabilities entry, or a required_skill, and only when a registered lane declares it. Pacing has two surfaces that do not share state: the router disables a lane only for claude (CLAUDE_DISABLED.flag via sync_default_registry) and for the codex/claude weekly spawn gate (GATED_AGENTS is codex and claude); AGY_LOW_QUOTA is read ONLY by execution consumers (agent_chain.vendor_gate, harvest), never by route_once. So a KIMI_LOW_QUOTA flag mirroring agy paces the chain but NOT the router unless kimi is also disabled router-side (claude pattern) or added to GATED_AGENTS. In agent_chain, vendors resolve from config/agent_chain.v1.json vendors plus roles tables and dispatch via a hardcoded vendor switch; kimi needs a config vendor block, a by_creator_vendor table, candidate rows in the other creators' critic lists, a VENDOR_ALIASES entry, a vendor_gate branch, resolve_cli/seat_env/model_id branches, and a run_kimi adapter. The Kimi-creator to non-Kimi-critic rule holds structurally because by_creator_vendor for kimi would list only non-kimi seats and cross_vendor is computed as seat.vendor not equal to creator_vendor. No gate/live/deployment/verdict authority is enforced by NOT declaring code/ops/scalpel_mechanization, NOT adding kimi to AGENT_TASK_TYPE_LANES, and keeping review_ea/close-review out of reach. Top risks mirror existing seats: Codex-style shared-token auth race (keep MaxSessions at 1 unless auth isolated), SYSTEM session-0 vs console-session DPAPI token access (agy/gemini hop via run_in_console_session.ps1), and agy-style stdin/TTY behavior (agy needs ConPTY plus pointer prompt; claude/codex read a stdin prompt file).

risks: Auth token race (Codex class): if the kimi CLI shares one OAuth/token file across processes, more than one concurrent session races on refresh and invalidates the login as codex did. Keep kimi orchestration MaxSessions at 1 unless per-session auth isolation exists. Evidence: install_agent_orchestration_scheduled_tasks.ps1:31-41.

Session-0 vs console session: scheduled tasks run as SYSTEM (session 0); agy/gemini hop to the qm-admin console via run_in_console_session.ps1 because the DPAPI/Credential-Manager token decrypts only in the operator context. Route kimi the same way if its auth is user-bound. Evidence: agy_governor.py:14-16; install ps1 gemini branch :68-82.

stdin/TTY handling (agy class): agy does not read stdin and hangs on non-TTY stdout, needing ConPTY plus a file-pointer prompt; claude/codex read a prompt file bound to stdin. Wrong pattern silently hangs the slot to timeout. Evidence: run_agent_orchestration_task.py:439-485, 879-888; agent_chain _run_agy :552-587.

Router-vs-execution pacing gap: a KIMI_LOW_QUOTA flag consumed only by agent_chain.vendor_gate will NOT stop the router from dispatching kimi orchestration tickets. Without a router-side disable or GATED_AGENTS membership, kimi keeps routing while nominally paced. Evidence: agent_router.py:1072-1074; route_once :1724-1976 reads no such flag.

Unroutable-capability trap: declaring only the 8 descriptive capabilities makes kimi idle. Add new task_types requiring them, or route research via payload required_capabilities / required_skills naming those strings (gate only because kimi declares them). Evidence: agent_router.py:106-128, :1770-1800.

Verdict/authority leakage: giving kimi code/ops/review/scalpel_mechanization caps, adding it to AGENT_TASK_TYPE_LANES, or letting it reach review_ea/close-review grants forbidden authority. Keep it research-only and REVIEW-terminal. Evidence: AGENT_TASK_TYPE_LANES agent_router.py:215-220; gemini no-self-approve :273-274; agent_chain.v1.json critique.skip_task_types review_ea.

Cross-vendor rule regression: if by_creator_vendor for kimi accidentally includes a kimi seat, the Kimi-to-non-Kimi invariant breaks (cross_vendor false). Preserve agy-last ordering. Evidence: agent_chain.py:258-269.

agy-class quality/hallucination risk: config brands agy research-only backup, never sole critic unless allow_agy. If kimi is a research backup, decide explicitly whether it may be a sole critic or mirror the allow_agy gate. Evidence: config/agent_chain.v1.json vendors._doc; open_critic_seats allow_agy :260-262.
unknowns: The kimi CLI: binary name/path, headless flags, whether it reads stdin or needs TTY/ConPTY, auth mechanism (API key env vs OAuth file vs Credential Manager), model ids. Not in the repo; determines resolve_cli, agent_env, command_for, seat_env, run_kimi, and the auth-race/session-0 mitigations.

Whether kimi is paced via the weekly-pace model (GATED_AGENTS plus model_matrix plus task_class in agent_quota_gate.v1.json) or the agy-style governor+flag. The NORMAL/CONSERVE/EXHAUSTED wording matches agy, but that alone does not pace the router.
Whether a kimi quota/usage telemetry source exists analogous to agy_quota.py or quota_pull.py. Without one a governor tracks only heuristically.

Whether kimi orchestration runs in a git worktree (codex/claude) or shared-repo (gemini), and its push/commit policy. A research-only REVIEW-terminal lane likely wants shared-repo plus no push, but this is a policy choice.

Exact new task_types (if any) to carry the 8 capabilities versus reusing research_strategy/review_strategy/agent_learn with payload required_capabilities. An OWNER/orchestrator routing-design decision.
